keys.default: (unset — the bot's lifecycle callbacks and the runtime's callbacks are refused with 401, bots get no internalSecret, and a recording upload needs a MeetingToken)
keys.description: shared secret for internal service-to-service calls. §1.10: meeting-api hands it to each bot (invocation internalSecret), POST /bots/internal/callback/lifecycle requires it as x-internal-secret, it keys the per-bot token in the runtime callbackUrl (POST /runtime/callback?t=<hex HMAC-SHA256 of "aw-runtime-callback.<workloadId>">; callback_auth.py), and a recording upload may present it as its bearer; every comparison is constant-time. Unset is a documented degrade; a PUBLISHED PLACEHOLDER is not — it is the whole internal tier handed to anyone who read the repository (F95), so the boot refuses it.

keys.default: (unset — every client route answers 401; the bot callbacks, /internal/*, /health and /metrics are unaffected)
keys.description: §1.10, §6.9 F-E: the key ring the gateway signs x-user-id with, the same ring the gateway holds, in the webhook secret encryption ring's format: JSON {"<kid>": "<exactly 32 bytes, base64>"}, a kid being 1-64 of A-Z a-z 0-9 . _ -. identity_guard.py checks x-gateway-signature: kid=<kid>,t=<unix>,v2=<hex HMAC-SHA256> under the key its kid names, over the kid, t, x-user-id and every other identity header the gateway forwards (email, scopes, limits, workspaces, webhook url, secret and events), method, body SHA-256, raw query and path (core/gateway/contracts/gateway-identity), and refuses with 401 a signature that is missing, malformed, under a kid not in this ring, wrong for any of those, or more than GATEWAY_IDENTITY_MAX_SKEW_S seconds from this clock. Unset or malformed, every client request is refused and the rejection log names the fault, never a key.

§1.10, §6.9 F-E: identity_guard.py refuses with 401 a gateway signature whose t is more than this many seconds before or after this service's clock (the replay window); the same setting on meeting-api and admin-api. Not a positive whole number, the guard is not built (a ValueError naming the setting) and no client request is served.

poll interval (s) of the transcription_segments stream consumer loop
db-writer cadence (seconds) — each tick flushes immutable live segments from the redis hash meeting:{id}:segments into the transcriptions table (the restored 0.10 flush loop)
parent-name alias for DB_WRITER_INTERVAL_S (0.10 collector env parity) — used only when DB_WRITER_INTERVAL_S is unset

how often (seconds) the db-writer runs its self-healing O(keyspace) meeting:*:segments SCAN — startup + every this-many seconds, off the DB_WRITER_INTERVAL_S hot path. The active_meetings set is authoritative in steady state; the per-tick scan saturated redis and starved /health, restarting healthy pods (#893)

how long (seconds) the db-writer keeps re-draining a FINISHED meeting's copilot processed-notes stream while waiting for the producing worker's view_end marker, before giving up loudly. The copilot's final beat runs ~10s after session_end and by then the meeting has left the active sweep, so without the parked re-drain those last notes stay in redis forever (ADR 0027)
seconds a live segment must sit unmodified before the db-writer flushes it to postgres — the still-mutable tail (drafts being refined) stays in redis until it settles (0.10 parity)

the hold (seconds) for a CONFIRMED Teams CSRC segment (source=merged plus speaker_key=csrc:<id>), whose drafts are explicitly retractable. Never raises the hold above IMMUTABILITY_THRESHOLD; pending Teams rows and every other lane keep the full hold
TTL (seconds) re-armed on the live segment hash meeting:{id}:segments at every append — an abandoned hash cannot linger forever once flushed (0.10 parity)
sweep interval (s) of the webhook retry-queue drain loop

webhooks (§2.7): comma-separated hosts a subscription delivery may target although they are private (compared case-insensitively, never resolved); the send-time SSRF guard (webhooks/ssrf.py) refuses every other private, loopback, link-local or internal target. admin-api applies the same list on save.

keys.default: (unset — with WEBHOOK_SECRET_ENC_ACTIVE_KEY also unset, no subscription delivery is signed or sent; deliveries wait in webhook_deliveries)
keys.description: webhooks (§2.7): the key ring subscription secrets are encrypted under, JSON {"<id>": "<32 bytes, base64>"} (AES-256-GCM; webhooks/secret_box.py), the same ring admin-api holds. meeting-api only decrypts, at signing time. Set with a malformed ring, a key that is not exactly 32 bytes, or without WEBHOOK_SECRET_ENC_ACTIVE_KEY, meeting-api refuses to start.

webhooks (§2.7): the id in WEBHOOK_SECRET_ENC_KEYS admin-api encrypts new secrets under. meeting-api decrypts with each row's own key id; this must still name a key in the ring, or meeting-api refuses to start.

webhooks (§1.8): cadence (s) of the outbox publisher (intake/outbox.py), single-flight across replicas: each tick turns up to 500 unpublished webhook_outbox rows into webhook_deliveries rows, one per matching active subscriber. It runs only with Postgres and ADMIN_API_URL + INTERNAL_API_SECRET (the subscription read); without them outbox rows stay unpublished.

webhooks (§1.8): cadence (s) of the subscription sender, one loop per replica (not single-flight: due webhook_deliveries rows are claimed FOR UPDATE SKIP LOCKED with a 60 s lease, so replicas share them). It runs only with Postgres, ADMIN_API_URL + INTERNAL_API_SECRET (the subscription read) and the WEBHOOK_SECRET_ENC_* key ring.

webhooks (§1.8, §6.9 F-A): the subscription sender's retry waits (s), comma-separated, 1 to 20 positive whole numbers. Its length is the number of retries: after a 5xx, 429, timeout, connection error, DNS timeout, too little lease left to post (lease short) or nothing to sign or resolve with, attempt n waits entry n; one failure after the last entry the delivery is dead (the default: 4 retries, 5 attempts). Set but malformed, meeting-api refuses to start.

webhooks (§1.8, §6.9 F-H): threads in the subscription sender's own DNS pool (the send-time SSRF guard's lookups), per replica; a whole number of at least 1. The pool is separate from the default executor recording storage uses, so slow DNS never delays recordings, and it is shut down on app shutdown. Set but malformed, meeting-api refuses to start.

webhooks (§1.8, §6.9 F-H): the most (s, above 0, decimals allowed) one send-time DNS lookup may take, waiting for a pool thread included. A lookup that takes longer is a failed attempt (error 'dns timeout') on WEBHOOK_RETRY_SCHEDULE_S. Set but malformed, meeting-api refuses to start.

webhooks (§1.8, §6.9 F-H): the most (s, above 0, decimals allowed) one subscription post may take in total; longer is a failed attempt (error 'timeout') on WEBHOOK_RETRY_SCHEDULE_S. Set but malformed, meeting-api refuses to start.

webhooks (§1.8): how long (whole s, at least 1) a sender's claim holds a delivery row before another replica may claim it again. It must be more than WEBHOOK_SEND_TIMEOUT_S + 5 s, so a claim can post and record inside it; a claim with less left sends nothing and records 'lease short'. Set but malformed, or too short, meeting-api refuses to start.
webhooks (§1.8): the most delivery rows (whole, at least 1) one sender tick claims; the rest wait for the next tick. Set but malformed, meeting-api refuses to start.
tick interval (s) of the schedule.v1 job loop (drives join-retry re-spawns)
grace (s) before a stopping meeting whose workload is gone is reconciled
interval (s) of the stop-reconcile loop
grace (s) before an active meeting with a dead workload is failed by the reconciler

grace (s) before a meeting whose bot has NOT yet reached the room (requested/joining/awaiting_admission) is reconciled — DERIVED from the lobby budget the spawn issues (VEXA_LOBBY_BUDGET_S, default 900s) plus 60s of headroom, so the control plane is never less patient than the deadline it handed the bot (#862, #1208)

lobby budget (s) issued to every spawned bot as automatic_leave.waitingRoomTimeout — how long it may wait for admission before reporting awaiting_admission_timeout. 15 min so an auto-joined bot outwaits a late host (#1208); the reconcile pre-active grace derives from it, so raising it never leaves a waiter reaped by a shorter watchdog. An explicit automatic_leave.max_wait_for_admission on POST /bots still wins.

continuous-untracked window (s): a meeting whose workload the runtime 404s for this long with no re-adoption and no bot callback is presumed lost and failed with an evidence note. Also §6.9 F-K2's proof-of-gone wait on a runtime 404, and the grace a waiting meeting or an unproven spawn gets past due_at.

JSON service-authority.v1 adapter config: credential-free endpoint URL, contract_version, timeout_ms, response_max_age_seconds, failure_policy=closed, and mode=enforce|observe. When set, unavailable or malformed authority decisions fail closed.
shared HMAC secret for exact-byte timestamped service-authority requests
poll cadence for due one-minute active-service decisions; boundary timestamps remain admitted_at + N minutes regardless of polling cadence

Boot-frozen operator destination for signed meeting.completed and bot.failed envelopes. It is never read from user or meeting data. HTTPS is required unless VEXA_SYSTEM_WEBHOOK_ALLOW_PRIVATE_HTTP explicitly enables an in-cluster HTTP service.
Shared secret for Bearer compatibility and exact-byte timestamped HMAC signing of the operator-owned terminal callback.
Explicit operator opt-in for an HTTP system callback on a private/in-cluster service network. This never changes the customer webhook SSRF policy.
Bounded HTTP timeout in seconds for the operator-owned terminal callback; must be greater than 0 and at most 60.
uvicorn bind host (lite binds 127.0.0.1 behind its internal proxy)
uvicorn bind port
uvicorn/app log level

keys.default: (unset — calendar sync no-ops and the auto-join sweep cannot resolve the per-user cap, so it fails closed and refuses to spawn unless AUTO_JOIN_ALLOW_UNCAPPED=1)
keys.description: admin-api base URL for the internal edges the background sweeps call (/internal/users/{id}/bot-context, /internal/calendar-configs). Required on every deploy surface so calendar sync runs and auto-join spawns stay capped (#656).
auto-join sweep cadence (s) — how often scheduled meetings are checked for a due start
auto-join lead (s) — the bot is sent this long before data.scheduled_at, so it is standing in the lobby at the scheduled start rather than setting out then (#1208). Deploy values may override.

auto-join grace (s) — an entry-less scheduled meeting older than this is never auto-joined (no hours-late joins); a meeting entries manage is due until its end instead (§1.5). The link resolver also uses it to ignore stale timed plans (an entry-less scheduled row past data.scheduled_at + this grace) on upstream planned edits (§1.6)
backoff (s) before an auto-join that failed loudly (cap/quota/spawn) is retried
not-sent sweep cadence (s, §1.5) — how often scheduled meetings that entries manage are checked for an end passed without a bot (they end failed, outcome not_sent)

keys.default: false — with no admin edge (ADMIN_API_URL/INTERNAL_API_SECRET) the per-user cap is unresolvable and the sweep fails closed (refuses to spawn); set 1 to deliberately allow uncapped self-host spawns
keys.description: opt-in escape hatch (#656): allow the auto-join sweep to spawn uncapped when the per-user cap cannot be resolved. Unsafe mode — chosen, never defaulted.
intake (§1.1 R3): PUT /v2/entries refuses an entry starting more than this many days ahead with too_far_ahead
intake (§1.1 R1) and POST /bots (§1.5): a join_now entry, or a POST /bots without a row id, adopts the earliest non-finished meeting on its link that hasn't ended and starts within this many seconds
intake (§1.3): comma-separated meeting-link hostnames refused with platform_not_enabled; empty ⇒ none refused
intake and auto-join (§6.9 F-K): an entry-managed meeting's bot send is tried at most this many times in total; the last failure ends the meeting not_sent with its typed code
intake and auto-join (§6.9 F-K): seconds between two sends of an entry-managed meeting's bot after a failure (entry-less rows keep AUTO_JOIN_RETRY_BACKOFF_S)
intake (§1.13): per-account quota of active entries (entries of unfinished meetings); a write that would add one past it is refused with 429 quota_exceeded
intake (§6.9 F-D): how many more times an entry write that lost a race on a database constraint is run again, after a short random pause; one that still loses answers 500 internal_error

entry service (§6.9 F-D): the least (s) of the random pause before an entry write that lost a constraint race runs again; the pause is a random point between this and INTAKE_CONFLICT_DELAY_MAX_S, times the try's number
entry service (§6.9 F-D): the most (s) of that random pause, before it is multiplied by the try's number

stop (§1.7): how many more times POST /v2/meetings/{id}/stop is run again when the meeting moved to another link between its read and its link lock; after the last, the stop answers 503 unavailable (retry)
intake sweeps (§6.9 F-I): the auto-join tick, the not-sent sweep and the outbox publisher read their work in pages of at most this many items, in a stable order, every page each tick

intake sweeps (§6.9 F-I): an item that fails this many times (counted per sweep in sweep_item_failures, across replicas) is logged, counted in aw_sweep_items_total{result=given_up} and never tried again by that sweep

§6.9 F-K2/F-I: how long (s) a workload's teardown is chased while the runtime doesn't answer before it is given up: a pending teardown (data.unproven_teardown) from its since, a stale-stopping or stale-nonterminal reconcile row from its updated_at. A runtime that doesn't answer is never one of the item's failures, so this age is its only bound; a refused delete still counts toward SWEEP_MAX_ITEM_FAILURES. Longer than any meeting (6 h)

§6.9 F-I: how long (s) a sweep_item_failures record untouched is kept; each reconcile pass deletes the older ones, SWEEP_BATCH_SIZE at a time (7 days). A given-up item's record is touched whenever its sweep still lists it, so only given-up items no longer pending go (their meeting gone or finished, their work cleared)
calendar-sync sweep cadence (s) — how often connected ICS feeds are re-fetched and upserted into planned meetings
#527: a background loop whose last heartbeat is older than this flips /health to degraded+503 (a hung consumer no longer looks alive)
#527: collector-group lag (unread transcription_segments) over this flips /health to degraded+503
#527: acked transcription_segments entries older than this are trimmed; an unread (un-acked) entry is NEVER trimmed regardless of age (the 2026-04-26 data-loss guard)
#636: per-replica Redis consumer name for the segment group; empty → derived as collector-<hostname> (pod identity) so a crashed replica's pending batch is attributable + reclaimable

#660: idle (ms) after which an abandoned per-recreate consumer (pending==0) is pruned from collector_group by the reclaim sweep (XGROUP DELCONSUMER); default 30 min, well above COLLECTOR_RECLAIM_MIN_IDLE_MS so a briefly-quiet live replica is never removed
#636: min idle (ms) before a replica reclaims another replica's un-acked segment batch via XAUTOCLAIM, so a live peer's in-flight batch is never stolen
#636: run the orphan-reclaim scan every N segment-consumer ticks
#636: /health degrades to 503 when the segment group's pending-entry (PEL) depth exceeds this — a stuck/orphaned batch is a reportable state (P18)

O-TEL-1: the captured-signal tape KEEP budget in bytes. Fixture collection is default ON, so the bound lives here rather than on the capture path — the janitor evicts oldest-unpromoted tapes under the `signal/` prefix until total tape bytes fit. Promoted tapes (a PROMOTED marker object beside them) are NEVER evicted; if promotion alone exceeds the budget the sweep deletes nothing and logs signal_tape_budget_unreclaimable for a human to decide
O-TEL-1: captured-signal budget sweep cadence (s) — one paginated listing of the `signal/` prefix plus per-object deletes, single-flighted across replicas
O-TEL-1: minimum tape age (s) before the budget janitor may evict it — the in-flight-upload guard, so a sweep firing mid-teardown can never half-delete a tape whose parts are still arriving

flows' intake, told when a bot this service dispatched goes active and when it completes (F168/F181 — an ad hoc bot started via the MCP request_meeting_bot never reached flows before this; only invite_intake's own emit_started/emit_completed, calendar-only, ever did). MEETING-API TELLS FLOWS; IT DOES NOT ASK IT — best-effort, bounded at 2s, swallowed (events.py), so a deployment with no flows domain runs meetings exactly as one with a flows domain does, and so does one where flows is down. Unset is a profile, not a degraded state. Spelled VEXA_FLOWS_API_URL to match agent-api's control_plane/config.v1.json (identity's admin-api spells the bare key FLOWS_API_URL for the same edge — the two publishers that already exist do not agree with each other; not fixed here).

operator key for the same edge, sent as X-Flows-Operator-Key (flows' POST /events is authenticated). Declared as part of the edge rather than beside it, on the same terms as identity's admin-api and agent-api's control_plane declare theirs: unset alongside an unset URL is the no-flows profile; unset with a URL set is a deployment whose facts are being refused.

stt.description: spawned bots can transcribe (the STT service bot_spawn threads into the invocation.v1 payload)
stt.when_unconfigured: POST /bots with transcribe_enabled=true answers a typed 503 naming the unset key(s) — bots must opt out explicitly (transcribe_enabled=false / TRANSCRIBE_ENABLED=false) to spawn capture-only

object_storage.description: recordings persist to the object store (chunk upload + finalize → meeting.data JSONB)
object_storage.when_unconfigured: recording upload/finalize fails at request time with a storage auth error; transcripts are unaffected
